findings.name: Technology Stack Identification (Angular & Heroku)
findings.description: The target application is identified as being built with Angular and hosted on the Heroku Platform as a Service (PaaS). This information is crucial for guiding subsequent penetration testing efforts towards known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations associated with these technologies.
findings.poc: Utilize this information to research common security vulnerabilities and misconfigurations associated with Angular applications (e.g., DOM XSS, insecure local storage, client-side routing issues) and Heroku deployments (e.g., exposed environment variables, insecure add-ons, buildpack vulnerabilities). No direct command is applicable for this type of OSINT beyond observation and further targeted research.

findings.name: Heroku Platform-Specific Security Considerations
findings.description: The application's deployment on Heroku indicates the need for specific security checks related to the Heroku platform. Potential vulnerabilities could arise from misconfigured buildpacks, improperly managed environment variables, or insecure add-ons.
findings.poc: Investigate common Heroku security best practices and potential misconfigurations. This includes looking for publicly exposed Heroku environment variables (e.g., through client-side leaks in JavaScript files), reviewing application logs for sensitive data exposure, and checking for insecure Heroku add-ons. While direct commands like `heroku config --app [app-name]` require authentication, the recon suggests areas for external investigation.

findings.name: Potential Hardcoded Secrets in Client-Side JavaScript
findings.description: Multiple client-side JavaScript chunk files are exposed, which is common in Angular applications. These files can sometimes contain hardcoded secrets, API keys, sensitive configuration data, or other credentials that should not be publicly accessible.
findings.poc: Download and analyze the content of each identified `chunk-*.js` file for patterns indicative of secrets. For example, use `curl https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/chunk-24EZLZ4I.js | grep -E '(api_key|secret|token|password|credentials|aws_access_key_id|db_user|jwt_secret)'` to search for common secret keywords. Manual review for obfuscated or less common patterns is also recommended.

agents.command: msfconsole -q -x "use auxiliary/scanner/http/http_login..." && hydra -L users.txt juice-shop.herokuapp.com http-post-form
amass enum -passive -d juice-shop.herokuapp.com && theHarvester -d juice-shop.herokuapp.com -b all
python3 cors_scanner.py -u https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com && python3 ssrf_scanner.py -u https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com
kr scan https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com -w routes-large.kite && restler --target https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com
cme smb juice-shop.herokuapp.com -u '' -p '' && bloodhound-python -d juice-shop.herokuapp.com -u null -p null -c All
subzy run --targets subdomains.txt && nuclei -tags takeover -u https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com
